title: Object construction & API design
literature: GoF creational; Effective Java (Bloch) builders/factories; fluent-interface (Fowler); Alexandrescu policy-based construction; dependency injection (Fowler).

members.name: Aggregate Instance
members.what: Bundle multiple related values into a struct and pass/return that aggregate by value instead of using several out-parameters.

members.name: Batch Method
members.what: An interface method operates on a whole set of elements per call (bulk get/set) rather than requiring one call per element.

members.name: Combined Method
members.what: Operations that clients commonly invoke as a sequence are combined into a single interface method executed as one unit (e.g. put-if-absent, open-and-read).

members.name: Construct On First Use
members.what: Access a static object only through a function that holds it as a function-local static, so it is constructed on the first call.

members.name: Dependency Injection
members.what: An assembler supplies a component's dependencies from outside (via constructor, setter, or interface) instead of the component constructing or locating them itself.

members.name: Design by Contract
members.what: Specify each routine's obligations as executable preconditions, postconditions, and class invariants, checked at runtime, with blame assigned by which side's clause failed.

members.name: Embedded Domain-Specific Language
members.what: A domain-specific vocabulary implemented as a library within a host language, reusing the host's syntax, types, and tooling instead of a separate parser.

members.name: Enumeration Method
members.what: A collection owner exposes a method that applies a client-supplied operation to each element internally, instead of handing out an external iterator.

members.name: Explicit Interface
members.what: A component's usage contract is captured in an interface type explicitly separated from any implementation class, so clients depend only on the declared interface.

members.name: Expression Builder
members.what: An object, or family of objects, that provides a fluent interface layered over a normal command-query API, translating chained expression-style calls into calls on the underlying objects.

members.name: Extension Interface
members.what: A component exports multiple role-specific interfaces reachable through a root interface (QueryInterface-style), rather than one ever-growing interface.

members.name: Facade/Backend Module Pattern
members.what: A module exposes a fixed facade API whose backend implementation is selected at build/link time per target platform.

members.name: Fluent Interface
members.what: An API designed so chained method calls read like flowing prose, building configuration or computation as an internal domain-specific language.

members.name: Function Control
members.what: Add a data parameter (enum, flag, mode value) to a function that selects which of several behaviors the function performs, letting one API entry point cover a family of variants without passing function pointers.

members.name: Functional Options
members.what: A constructor takes a variadic list of option functions, each of which mutates the value being configured; options are first-class values that can be composed, defaulted, and added without breaking callers.

members.name: Hardware Abstraction Layer
members.what: A stable set of interfaces that isolates application and middleware code from register-level hardware detail, so the same firmware runs across MCUs by swapping the layer beneath.

members.name: Immediate-Mode GUI
members.what: A GUI API style where user code re-declares the widgets to draw every frame inside the input/render loop (DoButton() each frame rather than CreateButton() once), with the library retaining little or no widget object state.

members.name: Introspective Interface
members.what: A component offers a separate interface through which clients can query metadata about its capabilities, properties, and configuration at runtime.

members.name: Lifecycle Callback
members.what: A framework or container invokes designated component methods at defined lifecycle transitions (initialize, activate, passivate, destroy), inverting control of lifecycle handling.

members.name: Named Parameter Idiom
members.what: Replace long positional parameter lists with a parameter object whose chained setter calls name each argument, passed to the real function.

members.name: Nifty Counter
members.what: A per-translation-unit static counter object ensures a shared static resource (e.g. std::cout) is initialized before first use and destroyed after last use across translation units.

members.name: Out-Parameters
members.what: Return data by writing through caller-supplied pointers, keeping the return value free for status.

members.name: Plugin
members.what: Links classes to an abstraction during configuration rather than compilation, so behavior is selected per deployment via configuration.

members.name: Product Trader
members.what: Clients create objects by naming an abstract product class plus a specification; a trader maps specifications to concrete product classes and performs the instantiation.

members.name: Retained-Mode GUI
members.what: A GUI/graphics API style where the library retains a persistent object model of the scene (widget tree/scene graph) that client code creates once and mutates, with the library handling redraws from the retained model.

members.name: Service Locator
members.what: Provide a global access point to a service through a locator that resolves the concrete provider at runtime, hiding both the provider's class and the lookup process.

members.name: Smart Constructor
members.what: A function that is the only exported way to build a value of an abstract type, performing validation or normalization so every constructed value satisfies the type's invariants.

members.name: Static Factory Method
members.what: A public static method returns instances instead of a public constructor, allowing naming, caching, subtype return, and non-instantiation.

members.name: Wrapper Facade
members.what: Concise, cohesive, type-safe class interfaces encapsulate low-level, non-portable system APIs (sockets, threads, mutexes) and their associated data.
